title: Grey Collars
mood: Sunlit, funny, a little salty. Arrival nerves, cheap food, warm people, first table duels with shaking hands. The biggest problem on the island is a ladder rank and a crush.
foreground: Dorm life in the Commons: Mama Odalys's kitchen, Nathan's volume, Baylee's silence, Inya's hoodie, Rana's scowl, Tomi's binder, Livvie counting credits.
Rowan's stage fright at a physical table versus his online name; small wins that cost real nerve.
Classes and grades, the ladder opening on Day 12, the Freshman Cup on Days 19-20 and the printed roster that reveals Inya's surname.
First meetings with every romanceable woman in her own place and at her own pace; town trips, the bonfire mixer, the pool, the night market.

Rowan's roommates and his neighbours on the bungalow row as real people the player can come to like — Nathan above all: loud, tactless, generous with snacks, loyal without knowing the word. Give each of them warm scenes, Nathan at least four. (One first-year of the row will not be here in Act 2. The game decides who in the night of Day 26; you do not know, so nobody may be singled out, shielded or mourned in advance.)
Chuck's stories as pure comedy. Viktor as a charming truant. Umbra House as a boarded-up curiosity on the ridge.
mustNotHint: Anything falling from the sky, anything cosmic, any dread about anybody. No foreshadowing of the bang before the Night slot of Day 26.
That anyone will be harmed. No comas, no curfews, no infirmary scenes beyond sunburn and a sprained wrist.
That Chuck's stories are true, that the tiles are records, that the Vault exists as more than 'old ruins'.
Lucian Marrow by name (he is a signature on a sponsorship plaque at most). Gideon is only a snob.
That the Charter is anything but a quaint school tradition.

title: The Morning After
mood: The same sunny school with one note out of tune. Excitement about the meteor, then a slow private unease that only someone sharing a room could feel. One bad dawn (Day 40) that the school explains away.
foreground: The bang as campus fun: Bex's stream, crater selfies, the cordon, wild theories. {H}'s triumphant return ({H=nathan?'told you cowards'|'{H:retLine}'}).
Roommate oddities in the bungalow, each small, each deniable. Never more than one per in-game day, never commented on by the narration.
{H} getting good — suspiciously, joyfully good — and {H=nathan?nicer|easier to be near}. People like the new {H} better. That should feel worse the longer it goes on.
School life at full strength: tryouts (Day 33), midterms (Days 47-49), Night of Masks (Day 54), romance routes opening.
Brant Kessler on Day 40: an ambulance cart at dawn, the word 'seizure', and Camille's face.
Viktor's search gathering pace; Umbra House becomes reachable; the pre-meteor mysteries (Chuck, Alpha cards, Hale) can be pursued in daylight.
mustNotHint: That {H} is dead (the body is unreachable before Day 60) or that '{H}' is not {H} — the narration never says so and no character concludes it before the player does.
The word 'Visitor', the words 'Hollow Duel', the Tessellate's rules. Nobody on the island has that vocabulary yet except Chuck, Oru and Ashdown, and they are not sharing.
Marrow in person (he lands Day 61). Gideon's reports.
That the Hollowed can be restored, or that an ante was involved. Day 40 looks medical.

title: Ward B
mood: Autumn storms. The school keeps smiling with its teeth. Curfew, rumours, a man in a grey suit, a ward that fills. The player's private unease becomes a secret he has to carry — and decide whom to share with.
foreground: The cracked crater crust and what lies under it (from Day 60). The weight of knowing while sharing a bungalow with it.
The second and third Hollowings, the curfew from Day 67, Camille's notes, Bex's stream being leaned on.
Marrow's arrival: charming, generous, everywhere. The Design Contest as a bright thing with his money behind it. Santángel's lab lights on late.
The Hale thread reaching Umbra House room 9; Ashdown's guilt; Josie's story; Silas's keys.
The Guest's rules becoming legible: the cold, the silence, the named ante, the fact that it pays and never cheats. Noor and the Charter.
Light still exists and matters: Promotion Duels, the North Crown friendly, the Winter Gala. Warmth is what is at stake, so show it.
mustNotHint: The way to win (ante 'everything you have taken', in the Vault). The pieces may be collected; nobody assembles them for the player.
That Aleksander Hale is alive in any sense, before the torn pages or the Vault are found.
Madame Oru's ancestry. She is still a night-market act with unsettling accuracy.
Gideon as second host. Who the Day-150 victim will be.

title: The Champion's Table
mood: Clear, cold term. The thing with the grey collar (or the white gloves) is climbing toward the Battle Team and everyone who can read a ladder can see it. Dread with a calendar. Allies form or do not.
foreground: Formal challenges to Battle Team members, one by one, each ante stranger and more intimate than the last.
The Island Open (Days 124-126): Rana's last chance, Livvie's money, Rowan's proof that he can play on a stage.
Lilia's hunger for a rival, and the Guest's dawning interest in 'the best'. Willas's pride. Day 150.
Marrow's endgame: the board vote, the crater glass in crates, the Archive count that does not add up, Viktor's temptation.
The Vault itself becoming reachable: the Gate, the sea cave, Chuck's confession, Oru's third reading.
Lantern Night (Day 139) as the last purely tender evening of the year.
mustNotHint: Which ending the player is heading for. Never signal that a choice 'locks' something.
That the Guest could choose to stay, leave or be recorded — those possibilities appear only inside the final duel's aftermath.
That Chuck cannot play in the Vault himself, until he says so (chuck_confided).

title: What Was Wagered
mood: Festival lights over a held breath. The Interschool Cup with a hollow in the middle of the home team, Founder's Festival night at the Ruin Gate, then either the quietest graduation the island has ever had or no graduation at all.
foreground: The Interschool Cup under strain: North Crown's honour, Isolde's offer, Rex's mistake.
Day 180: fireworks for Chuck's 75th on one side of the volcano, the Gate on the other. Everything the player gathered either is on the table or is not.
The final duel under the Charter's oldest reading, with a witness who counts.
Aftermath as long, earned scenes: wards emptying or not, a body brought home or not, what is done with a perfect record of a loud boy.
Finals, the Graduation Exhibition (Day 201), graduation, the last ferry.
mustNotHint: Nothing is withheld any more except by the characters' own reticence. Still: no narration verdicts, no 'this was the good ending'.
